scope: All twenty-eight chapter bodies of Thomas Aquinas’s Catena Aurea on Matthew in Mark Pattison’s Oxford English, edited by John Henry Newman. Three previously admitted complete sections (05-07-07, 09-23-26, 16-20-21) and five single-Father Advent excerpts are retained untouched, and 281 additional complete sections are admitted (284 complete sections replaying all 285 mechanical candidate blocks and covering all 1,070 canonical Clementine Matthew verses).
inspection: Inspected all 285 mechanical candidate blocks in candidates-fd372a66/candidates.json against the complete retained derivative text-130e334a/source.txt (7,215 lines: 28 chapter headings and 7,187 paragraphs). Verified every block’s opening and closing scripture lemmas and commentary boundaries directly against the held Clementine Vulgate, Douay-Rheims, and King James Matthew chapter files across chapters 1–28.

Verified all eight unparsed lemma lines in the CCEL transcription: line 3532 ('3l.' for 13:31), lines 3694, 4263, 4432, 4635, 5021, and 5737 ('l.' for verse 1 of chapters 14, 17, 18, 19, 21, and 24), and line 5927 ('[30]' for 24:30b). Retained all original wording and transcription defects unchanged.

Resolved two structural anomalies from direct reading of the commentary text. In chapter 5 (lines 1186–1216), the CCEL scripture heading prints only verse 14 while the commentary explicitly expounds verses 15 and 16 (lines 1200–1216), so section 05-14-16 carries canonical extent Matthew 5:14–16. At the chapter 15/16 boundary, mechanical block 177 (line 4090, ii.xv-p197) prints the bare lemma of Matthew 15:39 with no commentary before the Chapter 16 heading (line 4091), and Chrysostom, Augustine, and Rabanus expound 15:39 at the opening of mechanical block 178 (lines 4096–4099) before turning to 16:1–4; those two mechanical blocks are united as one cross-chapter section 15-39-16-04 (physical_line_ranges [[4090, 4090], [4092, 4114]], canonical extent Matthew 15:39–16:4).

Divided native verses keep their shared canonical verse number: 1:6, 1:8, 2:9, 6:10 (06-10-10a and 06-10-10b), 6:13 (06-13-13a and 06-13-13b), and 24:30; line 2064 prints both 7:24 and 7:25 in one paragraph. Two Clementine Vulgate vs. Oxford/KJV numbering divergences occur in Matthew and are anchored in canonical Clementine numbering: native 5:5 ('Blessed are the meek') maps to Clementine 5:4 and native 5:4 ('Blessed are they that mourn') maps to Clementine 5:5 (as noted in the Oxford edition at line 1070); in chapter 17, Clementine 17:14 unites KJV 17:14–15, so native 17:14–18, 17:19–21, 17:22–23, and 17:24–27 map to Clementine 17:14–17, 17:18–20, 17:21–22, and 17:23–26 respectively.
limits: This offline collation verifies the retained electronic derivative text-130e334a/source.txt and candidate index candidates-fd372a66/candidates.json (derived from xml-943a6b5f) and establishes all complete section boundaries and canonical Clementine extents. Inherited transcription defects and disputed internal attributions are preserved. No comparison to a printed facsimile, remote XML re-fetch, Latin critical text, or individual patristic originals is claimed. This edition’s coverage is distinct from the catalogue’s coverage of other commentators.
